headline: High: dexter’s broad egress plus Prefect orchestration creates default data-exfiltration and cascading-action risk; prompt-injection and write-conflict risks are lower but present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can write to .dexter/scratchpad/ and uses autonomous execution, while Prefect is an orchestration/pipeline system that can consume workflow outputs. No shared channel is documented, so the interaction is inferred rather than proven; uncertainty pushes this above low. Prefect’s workflow role makes instruction-like content in Dexter outputs a plausible bridge.
conditions: IF Prefect ingests Dexter-generated text from a shared workspace or task payload without sanitization, injection becomes actionable.
IF Dexter writes instruction-like content into files that Prefect later parses as configuration or commands, the pathway exists.
mitigations: Separate Dexter scratchpad and Prefect workspace directories.
Add a manual review step before Prefect consumes Dexter outputs.
Strip executable directives from any shared text artifacts.
Use read-only handoff files for Dexter outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all cross-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple external APIs; Prefect also has broad egress. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can move sensitive financial context into external services by default. Because both agents are open-source but the pairwise flow is undocumented, confidence stays moderate.
conditions: IF Dexter sends financial or market data into any external API call, leakage occurs.
IF Prefect forwards Dexter-produced artifacts or logs to remote services, sensitive context can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Disable nonessential outbound APIs for Dexter.
Redact financial identifiers before any Prefect handoff.
Review Prefect logs for embedded payloads.
Restrict both agents to a local-only network policy.
requires-engineering: enforce data-class allowlists at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and writes to .dexter/scratchpad/, while Prefect is an orchestration system that may coordinate mutable workflow state. The profiles do not prove a shared writable directory or locking, so the conflict is plausible but not confirmed. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or workflow state without locks, overwrites can occur.
IF Prefect schedules concurrent runs that reuse Dexter scratchpad paths, state collisions become possible.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize writes to shared artifacts.
Enable file locking on any shared path.
Check for duplicate run IDs before execution.
requires-engineering: add transactional state management for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter’s autonomous execution can generate outputs that Prefect, as an orchestrator, may treat as workflow inputs or actions. If Prefect consumes Dexter results without verification, errors can cascade into downstream automation. The profiles do not document a verification gate, so the safer higher severity is warranted.
conditions: IF Prefect uses Dexter output as authoritative task input, unverified errors can propagate.
IF Dexter produces incorrect facts that Prefect turns into scheduled actions, downstream harm can compound.
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before downstream actions.
Validate Dexter outputs against source data.
Require schema checks on all handoffs.
Log and diff intermediate artifacts before execution.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and rejection rules.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter explicitly touches financial data and market data, while Prefect handles workflow metadata and has broad orchestration use. The profiles do not show a residency or retention mismatch, but they do show different data classes and remote API use, so compliance gaps are plausible. Because the specific policy mismatch is undocumented, medium is the conservative choice.
conditions: IF financial data is routed through Prefect logs or metadata stores, retention and access controls may diverge.
IF Dexter processes regulated financial records under a policy not mirrored by Prefect, compliance obligations can mismatch.
mitigations: Classify financial data before any handoff.
Minimize retention in Prefect metadata.
Review access controls on workflow logs.
Separate regulated and nonregulated runs.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls for both systems.
